base: Use case: ads-marketing. Create ONE magnificent full-bleed landscape film frame, 16:9 aspect ratio, for a fictional 1950s American television commercial in a world of dinosaurs. Every element must be original. No text, no lettering, no numbers, no signatures, no logos, no frame, no montage or panels. No real celebrity likeness, existing characters, gore, or visible franchise references. Treat the absurd circumstances with absolute sincerity. All storytelling must be visible in one shot.

plume-ledger: Exquisitely hand-tinted large-format architectural photograph from a real-estate portrait studio in 1956; mist-green grass, persimmon brick and pearl gray sky. Wide three-quarter view of an immaculate little Miami split-level survivor base with a turquoise boomerang-shaped carport, a tall stone chimney, an egg-shaped mailbox, lovingly planted flowers, and a pet triceratops asleep curled beside the house. Early Florida morning, no people. Matte selenium shadows and pearl highlights; precise miniature-world specificity. House and pet centered; bottom sixth disposable for a caption.

1956 hand-tinted large-format advertising still life, deep chocolate velvet, mahogany and mint green. One beautiful antique folding large-format press camera with a black accordion bellows, engraved brass lens, chestnut wood frame, and silver cable release; emerging beside it is a small fan of blank-backed photographic prints and one print showing a tiny mint roofed house. Studio side light skims hardware, tactile darkroom paper. Hero camera centered in frame, straight-on three-quarter low angle. Rich soft luminous gelatin silver tones.

Aftermath of an overnight base raid as a dignified hand-tinted large-format landscape photograph. Miami morning, completely empty picturesque grass lot; lone tall weathered stone chimney at the middle, egg-shaped pastel turquoise mailbox still intact at right and a few red flowers. A sad small pet triceratops sits by the chimney like a dog awaiting its family. Absolutely no intact building, road, people, signs or letters. Pale warm sky, wistful selenium green and persimmon. Artful asymmetrical composition. Bottom sixth disposable for caption.
second-bell: 1950s field-and-stream sporting goods magazine gouache painting. Chestnut feathered Velociraptor with handsome ivory throat plume at heel beside a proud Black woman falconer wearing a red neck scarf and a waxed olive field jacket in an autumn meadow. She has a brass dog whistle on a thin cord, looks fondly down at her raptor. Luminous broken brush strokes, sap green and gold foliage, block-printed vermilion accents. Lifelike anatomy, powerful landscape composition with subjects on the right two thirds, shadows on the left.

1950s lavish sporting-goods gouache still life photographed for a cinema ad: one utilitarian cylindrical knurled brass dog whistle with distinct open mouthpiece, short loop and braided red lanyard coiling over bottle-green felt in a weathered wooden presentation case. Lower three-quarter product shot, brilliant golden rim highlights on brass, luscious illustrated material detail, exquisite cast shadow. Landscape. Whistle oversized centered. No marks anywhere.

A quietly comic finale for a 1950s sporting-goods advertisement in rich gouache, brushed detail, vermilion and hunter green. From inside a tidy American farmhouse looking outward through its open front door, an entire throng of at least nine eager feathered velociraptors crowd the porch, varying height, color and crest, all facing camera and craning in like polite dogs awaiting invitation. Red doormat, autumn meadow beyond, warmly lit by sunset. No humans. Absolutely straight-faced naturalist illustration with clear, expressive animal silhouettes.
strata-supper-club: 1950s Parisian-American high dining advertising lithograph for a restaurant beneath the world. Elegant woman in a 1950s saffron day dress with shopping bag, caught floating gently downward through a clean glitch gap in a Miami sidewalk, her skirt billowing modestly like a parachute. A clear cutaway shows blue sky, pastel apartment towers and pavement above, aubergine empty air below; the legs of a tiny dodo remain on the intact sidewalk. Whimsical, confidently drawn, excellent silhouette and beautifully controlled shapes, brush ink, gold and raspberry gouache. Wide cinematic picture; woman entirely visible in the center.

Interior of the world's most glamorous 1950s supper club, underneath a floating Florida city; vista through immense panoramic dining window reveals the incredible underside of the world, rock islands with dangling roots, pipes, upside-down skyscraper foundations, empty violet twilight. Foreground an elegantly set curved banquette with a pair of glowing lamps, champagne flutes and a single immaculately set table, plum velvet, ochre and rose. Small feathered dinosaur maître d’ in silhouette attending the table in the far right. Painterly fashion gouache and brush ink, lavish cosmopolitan scene. Landscape.

1950s American restaurant dessert advertisement; close-up of an extravagant jewel-like layered pink grapefruit parfait crowned by a glossy cherry in a delicate stem glass on plum damask with silver spoon and ivory napkin, and one remarkable upside-down wafer shaped like a miniature city skyline descending into the cream. Raspberry, saffron, aubergine. Creamy gouache, woodcut outlines, gourmet brochure finesse. Crop tight with parfait on the right, softly shaded left. No decoration resembling letters.
tickaway-motor-tours: Classic 1950s four-ink Florida travel lithograph, wonderful sense of scale, more painterly than geometric clip art. A vivid teal and ivory unmarked 1950s excursion bus with sweeping fins and rounded windows parked beside a pink stucco hotel on a Miami boulevard under a tall palm tree. In foreground to the right is a small orange mechanical parking meter. Early morning coral light, sun-bleached aquamarine, long blue-violet shapes. Show the whole bus side on from slight low angle. No text, no hotel signs, no bus route numbers or painted characters.

1950s Florida tourism illustration, vibrant four-ink lithographic flat color with beautifully observed painterly figures. Inside an unmarked teal excursion bus, a cheerfully unflappable uniformed woman tour guide in a pale coral cap holds a 1950s silver microphone and gestures grandly out the window at a pink Miami art-deco hotel, orange parking meter and single huge palm tree just outside. Three curious passengers in period sun hats and a small dodo riding on a lap. Wide, characterful composition. Sea-glass teal, coral and lemon. No lettering or signs.

Tourist souvenir from 1950s Miami, a vibrant travel lithograph of a still life on peach-colored hotel stationery: big gleaming coral and brass mechanical parking meter head with a simple solid red expired wedge and no legible lettering; in the background an unmarked teal-and-cream rounded tour bus still sits in front of a small pink stucco hotel and the same tall palm tree at sunset. Dramatic close focus on the meter, cinematic shallow perspective, optimistic hand-pulled screenprint colors teal, purple and melon. No words, numbers or symbols anywhere.
fussbudget-feed: Lavishly painted 1950s American food magazine cover art without type, saturated butter yellow, blue and tomato red. In a spotless chrome-trimmed kitchen, a tuxedo-patterned baby tyrannosaurus with little down feathers sits at a yellow counter on the left, staring skeptically at a grand buffet of individually different colorful kibble balls arranged on a tiered silver tray offered by an anxious chef in a starched jacket on the right. The chef uses polished silver tongs; rich egg tempera illustration, precise faces, plausible limbs. Whole tender little scene, eye-level kitchen photography composition. No printed packaging.

1950s Technicolor food studio advertising shot, sumptuous three-quarter close-up: an open grand bonbon sampler box, powder blue exterior and blood-orange satin folds, each compartment filled with differently colored dry gourmet dinosaur kibble bites shaped like little round dumplings in paper cups; one bone-shaped brass clasp. Chrome studio countertop, vivid edge lights, perfectly appetizing analog commercial photography. Box fills frame diagonally. No text or logos or stray utensils.

Painted American food advertisement scene in the buttery light of a midcentury suburban kitchen. A tiny cream and brown feather-down baby tyrannosaurus sits by the kitchen door proudly offering its red leather walking lead in its mouth to a startled chef in a white jacket and blue trousers. The open box of dozens of colorful gourmet kibble bonbons sits conspicuously abandoned on the counter. Emphasize the dangling loop handle of the leash by the little dinosaur's mouth, a sweet imploring look; the leash must be hand-walk sized. Sunny yellows, cobalt, and tomato red, egg tempera magazine illustration. No text.
velvet-rope-appeals: Black-and-white 1950s television studio noir still, dramatic chiaroscuro, medium wide composition. A wet city sidewalk outside closed brass-and-frosted-glass double doors, a tiny startled dodo in a bowler hat stands outside on the pavement with a plain manila folder under one wing, its reflection in rain. Inside the tall doors blurry warm light suggests a government appeals office. Wet stone, silver shadows, film grain; dodo has a hooked beak, pudgy flightless body, short legs. No signs, letters or symbols; clean unmarked glass. Right-center foreground subject.

Black-and-white 1950s television noir advertising photograph with exquisite silver gelatin lighting. On a government clerk's dark desk an ornate brass queue bell, a stack of blank docket forms with line rules but no letters, a fountain pen and a velvet rope barrier softly out of focus in background. One sharp pool of side light, generous silver highlights, near-black corners, exquisite macro detail. Make queue bell the hero, an overhead three-quarter angle. No text or visible letters, no modern devices.

Black-and-white 1950s television noir still. Interior of an enormous Art Deco appeals office. One plainly empty visitor chair under a dramatic narrow shaft of window light, centered front. At the back far past a zigzag of velvet ropes, a plump officious small dodo clerk wearing a neatly tied dark bow tie waits behind a very high marble counter. Clever scale contrast, office utterly empty; classic perspective and impeccable silver-gelatin shadows. No writing anywhere. Wide symmetrical architectural composition.
